bookOpen.subtitle: Here we go… a few little moments from our story, just as I remember them. Let's start where we were only classmates.

holdReturn.subtitle: We've paused here. Take your time. You can take my hand again, switch to hands-free, or leave—whatever feels right. No need to explain.

scenes.title: A quiet beginning
scenes.subtitle: Hi, Nidhi… I made a little world out of some memories I still keep close. If you'd like, take my hand and let's step inside together. No rush—you can pause, let go, or leave whenever you want.
scenes.text: Hi, Nidhi. I made a little world out of some memories I still keep close. If you'd like, take my hand and let's step inside together. No rush—you can pause, let go, or leave whenever you want.
scenes.alt: A dark theater stage where a warm spotlight clicks on, the narrator drops in from above, slowly stands up looking at Nidhi, waves hi, and reaches his hand toward the bottom-right corner.

scenes.title: Before we really noticed each other
scenes.subtitle: Back then, we were just classmates—nothing more. During online classes, I was usually half-asleep and barely paying attention. When school was back in person, I stayed with my friends at the back. We hardly noticed each other.
scenes.text: Back then, we were just classmates—nothing more. During online classes, I was usually half-asleep and barely paying attention. When school was back in person, I stayed with my friends at the back. We hardly noticed each other.
scenes.alt: First a sleepy morning online class on a laptop, then a sunlit Class Seven and Eight classroom with back benches and a drifting paper airplane.

scenes.title: The paper house
scenes.subtitle: Then Sir put us in the same science-project group. We made little houses for the series and parallel circuits. I worked on the electrical part, and you made the tiny paper sofa and bed. When you sent me that picture on Messenger, it was our first real interaction. Such a cute little beginning.

scenes.title: Across the rooftops
scenes.subtitle: I was singing with my cousins on our rooftop, and you saw us from your balcony. You asked our friend if that was my house, then sent me a snap. I sent one back. A song, two snaps—and suddenly we had a reason to talk.

scenes.title: Our own little language
scenes.subtitle: Then came the good-morning messages, the rooftop and balcony glances during power cuts, and those matching steps across the distance. Coaching together, teasing each other, sometimes sneaking off for food… Little by little, we became best friends.

scenes.title: The river and our very detailed plan
scenes.subtitle: I planned that river outing almost minute by minute—boat ride, sunset, back in time. The boat renter surprised us with a huge overcharge, so we paid and left. On the rickshaw ride back, we mostly just looked at each other. Not quite the plan I had imagined… but a memory I still love.

scenes.title: Best friends, before we had the words
scenes.subtitle: I used to tell you I thought nobody would choose me. You'd say, 'Be patient.' And there I was, acting like your love teacher, even though I'd never been in love. Whenever you said someone would love me someday, I quietly hoped you meant you.

scenes.title: The silence, and finding our way back
scenes.dateLabel: Two quiet days; exact date unknown
scenes.subtitle: I thought people were misunderstanding how close we were, so I made distance instead of talking honestly with you. Then came two quiet days. I should have explained myself with more care. I'm sorry for how I handled that.
scenes.text: I thought people were misunderstanding how close we were, so I made distance instead of talking honestly with you. Then came two quiet days. I should have explained myself with more care. I'm sorry for how I handled that.
scenes.alt: Two still windows across a quiet dusk street as two silent days pass.

scenes.title: The chocolate wrapper
scenes.subtitle: I had kept and framed the wrapper from the chocolate you gave me. I sent you a snap of it, and you asked if we could go back to how we were. We started talking again and found our way back to being best friends.

scenes.title: The night our feelings had words
scenes.dateLabel: November 2023; after November 10; exact day unknown
scenes.subtitle: Sometime in November 2023, after my birthday, we were on a regular night call. Then the words finally came: 'I love you.' We never pinned down the exact date. Maybe that's okay—our story had been growing for a long time before those words.

scenes.title: All the little chapters after that
scenes.subtitle: Messages, photos, letters, calls, jokes… so many little chapters. I couldn't fit them all in this book. These are just a few of the memories I wanted to keep close.

scenes.title: What I am sorry for now
scenes.subtitle: Recently, I said we should break up, and I said, 'I don't love you anymore.' Those were my words, and I know they could hurt deeply. I'm sorry. Whatever I was feeling doesn't excuse saying them.
scenes.text: Recently, I said we should break up, and I said, “I don't love you anymore.” Those were my words, and I know they could hurt deeply. I'm sorry. Whatever I was feeling doesn't excuse saying them.
scenes.alt: A quiet pool of warm light where the narrator stands with honest accountability, plus an optional playful foam-helmet cartoon bonk.

scenes.title: What changes after this
scenes.subtitle: I want to pause before I speak when I'm upset, talk about my feelings without threatening our relationship, listen when I've hurt you, and respect the time or space you need. This game can't prove that. My actions have to.

scenes.title: An open ending
scenes.subtitle: This flower is just a small gift—no answer needed. Thank you for the paper sofa, the rooftop songs, the river sunset, and all the little moments that became ours. I'm sorry, Nidhi. You can close the book here, and I'll respect whatever you need.
